source: TSTD project (TA 7305-CAM), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំពោត" (Corn Cultivation Technical Manual), Section 3.b: Irrigation/watering, May 2012
text:
Farmers should keep the field consistently moist, watering regularly, and pay particular attention during the plant's critical early growth stage (from about 1 to 1.5 meters tall). During this stage, farmers should make sure the topsoil does not dry out and crack, and should also drain away any excess standing water so roots do not rot.

Water is one of the most important factors for corn productivity, and the quality of the water source matters as much as the quantity, especially water used for spraying onto the crop -- if contaminated or poor-quality water is used for spraying, it can damage the crop.
